To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PEDV is still circulating in China and that the S gene of the PEDV circulating in China recently is a variant of the S gene of KNU-serial PEDV strains.
a novel variant PEDV is responsible for clinical diarrhea in suckling pigs in China.

PEDV was detected by RT-PCR in samples collected from pig farms in China, and phylogenetically, the M genes were clustered in cluster 3 with Korean, Thai and Chinese strains, while the S genes were grouped in cluster 2 with Korean KNU-sequential strains and clustered in cluster 2 and 3 with Chinese and Korean strains, respectively.

the genetic characterization of PEDV field isolates in China.
the molecular epidemiology of the PEDV field strains that were circulating in China during 2009-2010.
the genetic diversity of PEDV field isolates in China and the molecular epidemiology of PED.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PEDV strains with a characteristic variant genome are circulating widely in China, and the PEDV field strains are closely related to Korean KNU strains.
the PEDV field strains prevailing recently are similar to the KNU-serial strain, but different from previous PEDV strains.
PEDV field strains prevailing recently are genetically different from those reported previously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a PEDV variant with a novel S gene is circulating in pig farms in China.
PEDV strains in China are evolving and that PEDV field strains with a novel variant S gene have been circulating widely.
PEDV is still a serious disease of piglets in China, and that the PEDV strains circulating in recent years are different from those in the 1980s.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEDV strains circulating in China are closely related to Korean PEDV strains.
a PEDV field variant strain is circulating in China and that it may be responsible for the recent outbreaks of PED.
the novel PEDV strain with a characteristic variant of the S gene has been prevalent in China in recent years.
